title: Chevalley Lie data with a full-weight admissible representation
statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional rational vector space and $R\subset V\setminus\{0\}$ a reduced crystallographic root system, with rational coroot functionals $ ar c_\alpha$ and weight lattice $P$ in the explicit conventions of [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding]. There exist a finite-dimensional split semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ over $\mathbf Q$ [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ (a maximal abelian subalgebra whose adjoint operators are simultaneously diagonalizable), an identification $\mathfrak h^\vee\simeq V$, and root vectors $e_\alpha\in\mathfrak g$ with $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus igoplus_{\alpha\in R}\mathbf Qe_\alpha$. Under $\mathfrak h\simeq V^\vee$, put $h_\alpha= ar c_\alpha$. For a simple-root base $\Delta$ (a basis of $V$ such that every root has integral coefficients all nonnegative or all nonpositive), the $h_\delta$ and $e_\alpha$ form a Chevalley basis: $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha$, $[h,e_\alpha]=\alpha(h)e_\alpha$, and, for $\alpha+ eta
e0$, the bracket is zero if $\alpha+ eta
otin R$ and is $\pm(p_{\alpha, eta}+1)e_{\alpha+ eta}$ otherwise, where $p_{\alpha, eta}$ is the largest integer $p\geq0$ with $ eta-p\alpha\in R$. There also exist a faithful Lie representation $ho:\mathfrak g	o\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf Q}(W)$ and a full lattice $\Lambda\subset W$ (a finite-rank free abelian subgroup with $\Lambda\otimes\mathbf Q=W$). Its weight decomposition is $W= igoplus_{\lambda\in\Omega}W_\lambda$, where $\Omega\subset P$ is finite, $W_\lambda
e0$, and $ho(h)w=\lambda(h)w$ on $W_\lambda$. One has $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$ and $\Lambda= igoplus_{\lambda\in\Omega}(\Lambda\cap W_\lambda)$. Each $ho(e_\alpha)$ is nilpotent and each divided power $D_{\alpha,m}=ho(e_\alpha)^m/m!$, $m\geq0$, preserves $\Lambda$. For $R=\varnothing,V=0$, one may take $\mathfrak g=0$, $W=\mathbf Q$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, $\Omega=\{0\}$.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.63 and its rational-field extension, pp.503--508; Chevalley bases and Theorem 23.71, pp.508--509; admissible lattice and equation (152), p.510; full-weight choice in Corollary 23.73, p.511.

proof.text: If $R=\varnothing$, the spanning hypothesis gives $V=0$. Take $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h=0$, $W=\mathbf Q$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ and $\Omega=\{0\}$. The map from the zero Lie algebra is injective, the empty Chevalley basis is a basis of zero, and the only divided-power requirement is vacuous since there are no roots. All lattice and weight identities follow immediately. Henceforth $R\ne\varnothing$.

Apply [lem-sfb-serre-rational-presentation] to the given rational root system and choose a simple base $\Delta$. Its actual Serre quotient $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak s(A)$ has splitting Cartan $\mathfrak h$ with $H_i\mapsto\bar c_{\alpha_i}$ and root spaces indexed by the given $R$. Prescribe the generator $E_i$ in each simple-root space, and apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-root-normalization] to extend these to $e_\alpha$. This keeps the coroot identification and supplies the required bracket constants. Since the root spaces are one-dimensional, these vectors together with the $H_i$ are the required basis. Dualizing the supplied Cartan identification gives $\mathfrak h^\vee\simeq V$.

source.place: Theorem 23.63, pp.503--504, characteristic-zero extension p.508; Chevalley bases and Theorem 23.71, pp.508--509

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-highest-weight-modules] to this split rational algebra and its simple base. Under the Cartan identification its weight lattice is exactly the prescribed $P$, since its coroot elements are $\bar c_\alpha$. The fundamental weights $\omega_i$ form an integer basis of $P$. For each $i$ take $L_i=L(\omega_i)$ and a highest vector $v_i$, and form $W=\bigoplus_i L_i$ with componentwise Lie action $\rho$. Its nonzero weight spaces are the sums of the corresponding summand weight spaces, so its finite weight set $\Omega$ lies in $P$ and contains every $\omega_i$. Therefore $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$.

source.place: Section 23h, p.508 (weight gradations) and proof of Corollary 23.73, p.511; highest-weight input made explicit

proof.text: The representation just constructed is faithful. Its kernel $I$ is an ideal, by the representation identity of [def-wf-lie-algebra]. It is stable under every $\operatorname{ad}h$. Choose rational $h_0\in\mathfrak h$ on which the finitely many distinct functionals $0$ and $\alpha\in R$ have distinct values: on a rational basis use vectors $(1,t,\ldots,t^{r-1})$, avoiding the finitely many integer roots of their nonzero difference polynomials. For each eigenvalue $a$, the polynomial $\prod_{b\ne a}(\operatorname{ad}h_0-b)/(a-b)$ projects onto its eigenspace and preserves $I$. Thus $I=(I\cap\mathfrak h)\oplus\bigoplus_\alpha(I\cap\mathbf Qe_\alpha)$. An $h\in I\cap\mathfrak h$ annihilates every $v_i$, so every $\omega_i(h)=0$; their rational span is $\mathfrak h^\vee$, hence $h=0$. If $I$ contained a nonzero root component it would contain $e_\alpha$, and therefore $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha\ne0$, contradicting $I\cap\mathfrak h=0$. Hence $I=0$.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.509--511; elementary verification of faithfulness of the chosen direct sum

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-kostant-integral-pbw] for the Chevalley basis just fixed. For each $i$ define the actual subgroup $\Lambda_i=U_{\mathbf Z}v_i\subset L_i$, where the enveloping action is the extension in that node. By its integral triangular basis, $\Lambda_i$ is the integer span of the vectors $\prod_j e_{-\beta_j}^{(a_j)}v_i$. Indeed every nonidentity positive factor kills $v_i$, and each Cartan binomial acts on $v_i$ by $\binom{\omega_i(H_k)}{b_k}\in\mathbf Z$ (here $\omega_i(H_k)$ is $0$ or $1$). Conversely each negative product belongs to $U_{\mathbf Z}$. The rational span of $\Lambda_i$ is all $L_i$: it contains $v_i$ and is stable under all root operators, hence their brackets $H_k$, which span $\mathfrak g$ together with the root vectors; the highest-weight module is cyclic. By definition $U_{\mathbf Z}\Lambda_i\subseteq\Lambda_i$, so every divided root power preserves $\Lambda_i$.

source.place: Section 23h, p.510, admissible lattice before equation (152); integral triangular-basis argument

proof.text: This generating family is finite after zero vectors are removed. A negative monomial of multi-degree $a$ applied to $v_i$ has weight $\mu=\omega_i-\sum_j a_j\beta_j$, by repeated use of $[h,e_{-\beta_j}]=-\beta_j(h)e_{-\beta_j}$. In simple-root coordinates each positive $\beta_j$ has height at least one. If the vector is nonzero, $\mu$ is among the finite weights of $L_i$, so $\sum_j a_j\le\operatorname{ht}(\omega_i-\mu)\le B_i$, where $B_i$ is the maximum of these finitely many nonnegative integers. There are finitely many tuples $a$ with this bound. Moreover the surviving generators are homogeneous weight vectors. Grouping an integer linear combination by weight therefore proves $\Lambda_i=\bigoplus_\mu(\Lambda_i\cap(L_i)_\mu)$.

source.place: Section 23h, p.510, construction of an admissible lattice and equation (152), with finite-generation bound written out

proof.text: Choose a rational basis of $L_i$. The finitely many generators of $\Lambda_i$ have rational coordinates, so one positive integer $d$ clears all denominators and embeds $d\Lambda_i$ as a subgroup of $\mathbf Z^{\dim L_i}$. By [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free], $\Lambda_i$ is free of finite rank. Its integer basis is rationally independent by clearing denominators in any rational relation, and rationally spans $L_i$ by Step 5. Consequently $\Lambda_i\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q\simeq L_i$. Take $\Lambda=\bigoplus_i\Lambda_i\subset W$. The finite direct sum is full, free, preserved by every componentwise divided root power, and decomposes into its weight intersections by Step 6.

source.place: Section 23h, p.510, definition of lattice and equation (152); finite-free subgroup input

proof.text: Finally $\rho(e_\alpha)W_\mu\subseteq W_{\mu+\alpha}$: for $w\in W_\mu$, the representation identity gives $\rho(h)\rho(e_\alpha)w=\rho(e_\alpha)\rho(h)w+\alpha(h)\rho(e_\alpha)w=(\mu+\alpha)(h)\rho(e_\alpha)w$. Since $\alpha\ne0$, the weights $\mu+n\alpha$ are distinct as $n$ varies. The weight set is finite, so every sufficiently long iteration is zero, with one common bound for the finite set $\Omega$. Thus every root operator is nilpotent. Its $m$th divided power is the enveloping action of $e_\alpha^{(m)}$, already shown to preserve $\Lambda$; $m=0$ is the identity. This supplies all remaining requirements.

source.place: Section 23h, p.509, nilpotent root operators; p.510, admissibility

proof_origin.place: Section 23h, pp.503--511; follows the Serre/Chevalley/highest-weight route, with the integral PBW construction and elementary assembly written by NZ. Missing deeper sources recorded WANTED in report.md.
